evidence.quote: one (1) or more tracts of land in Indiana

summary.short: Indiana state gross retail and use tax exemption for equipment sold to qualified data centers and to quantum, advanced-computing and defense networks, conditional on a corporation-issued award certificate and agreement. Local payments apply from mid-2026; an impact study is due from 2030.
summary.long: Chapter 15 of IC 6-2.5 exempts from state gross retail tax the sale of qualified data center equipment, and of quantum computing, advanced computing and defense network equipment, to a qualified user approved by the Indiana Economic Development Corporation (IC 6-2.5-15-16). Eligibility requires a specific transaction award certificate, expiring within 25 years (50 years for larger investments), and an agreement with the corporation (IC 6-2.5-15-14, -15). Qualified data centers must create minimum investments of $150 million, $100 million or $25 million, depending on county population (IC 6-2.5-15-10); the defense network threshold is $50 million (IC 6-2.5-15-13.4). Buyers provide sellers an exemption certificate and a copy of the award (IC 6-2.5-15-17). For permits and certificates after June 30, 2026, a user in a local unit pays up to 1% of the taxes not paid on quarterly electricity billings to the county or municipal fiscal officer (IC 6-2.5-15-15.5). The corporation may request assessment of unpaid taxes, with interest and penalties, after noncompliance (IC 6-2.5-15-18). Awards survive transfer of the facility (IC 6-2.5-15-19). From 2030 and every ten years, the corporation submits an economic and fiscal impact study to the legislative council (IC 6-2.5-15-20).

notes: Text is an Indiana Code 2026 compilation with revisor's notes and history notes; amendments are identified only from those notes. Several sections carry revisor's notes that their effective dates were changed to 1-1-2026 by P.L.213-2025, SEC.337. The chapter uses the term department without defining it; IC 6-2.5-15-15.5(c) refers to the state department of revenue. IC 6-2.5-15-15.5 applies only to permits issued and certificates issued after June 30, 2026. Section 20 requires the first study beginning in 2030 and every ten years thereafter. Statutory amounts and thresholds are coded in other sections of this annotation, not here.
